verdict.root_cause: checkout crashes inside its own code: retained logs show Go runtime panics (nil pointer dereference / SIGSEGV) raised in the send-to-post-processor path reached from the PlaceOrder handler, with identical faulting address and program counter at both ends of the week [tr_6943c47a6092]. This is a reproducible defect in the artifact checkout is running, not propagated downstream failure — no downstream error status is in the stack, and sampled traces show currency, payment, shipping, cart and email legs all completing in milliseconds [tr_220bfd64ac6d]. A panicking PlaceOrder handler explains checkout alerting first at 05:18:31 and frontend-proxy following two minutes later as the caller observing the broken RPC. The CURRENCY_ADDR flapping on checkout sits ~46.5h before onset and ended in the reverted (unset) state, so it was not the value in effect at onset [tr_4107f89ed02e], and currency itself has no recorded change at all [tr_2754c2f01980].
verdict.reasoning: The only positive failure signal anywhere on the board is checkout's own panic, localized to a named source line in checkout application code, recurring with identical addr/pc — a defect in the running build rather than a transient or environmental condition [tr_6943c47a6092]. Dependency slowness is contradicted by the trace sample, where all checkout children are short and complete [tr_220bfd64ac6d]. The config angle is the natural competitor but is time-misaligned and left in the reverted state [tr_4107f89ed02e], and currency shows no change at all [tr_2754c2f01980]. Confidence is low because no deploy or release record for checkout exists in the window [tr_4107f89ed02e] and both metric attempts failed with HTTP 400, so error rate and traffic around 05:18:31 are entirely unmeasured [tr_e1b6682a980d, tr_4d375df5a94e].
open_questions: No deploy record for checkout appears in the change log, so the artifact-version claim is inferred from the panic's reproducibility rather than observed; when did the faulting build start running?
Both metric queries were rejected with HTTP 400, leaving checkout's error ratio and request rate at onset unmeasured [tr_e1b6682a980d, tr_4d375df5a94e].
No traces from at or before 05:18:31 were returned (sample truncated, 5 of 10, all from 2026-10-11) so the onset cohort was never inspected [tr_220bfd64ac6d].
Whether an unset CURRENCY_ADDR is what leaves the nil pointer in the post-processor path — the config flap and the panic site may be the same story.

alternatives.root_cause: The CURRENCY_ADDR environment variable was left unset by the last automated revert, and checkout dereferences a nil client built from that missing address.
alternatives.why_not: The last edit predates onset by ~46.5 hours with a two-day quiet period before the incident, and the panic signature already appears on 2026-10-07, before the flapping window [tr_4107f89ed02e, tr_6943c47a6092].

alternatives.root_cause: currency-service became slow or unreachable and checkout failed while waiting on Convert.
alternatives.why_not: Both Convert calls complete in 0.6-9.7ms with matching peer spans in every sampled trace, and checkout's stack shows a nil dereference in its own frame with no downstream error status [tr_220bfd64ac6d, tr_6943c47a6092].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in checkout's panic rate, error ratio, or frontend-proxy's 5xx rate should be observed. The named fix class (rollback) cannot be executed: rollback_image requires both a prior image tag in change history and evidence of a deploy or image change inside the window, and [tr_4107f89ed02e] states the change log for checkout contains no deploy or release entries at all — only eight CURRENCY_ADDR environment edits — so the artifact-version claim is inferred from panic reproducibility, not observed. restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state; [tr_6943c47a6092] shows the opposite: an identical faulting address and program counter at both ends of a week in the send-to-post-processor path reached from PlaceOrder, which is a deterministic code defect that a container recreate will reproduce on the next PlaceOrder. revert_config has a recorded prior configuration but fails its second precondition — the nearest CURRENCY_ADDR edit sits ~46.5h before onset with a two-day quiet period before 05:18:31, and the final recorded state is the reverted (unset) one, so invoking it would re-apply CURRENCY_ADDR=currencyservice:7001, a value explicitly ruled out as in effect at onset and a change rather than a restoration.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if a deploy record for checkout inside the window is found in a source not yet queried (the change-log query was untrusted and scoped to one window), or if a corrected metric query — the two attempts returned HTTP 400 and measured nothing [tr_e1b6682a980d, tr_4d375df5a94e] — shows checkout's error ratio stepping at 05:18:31 rather than running elevated across the whole week. The panic-reproducibility evidence spans 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-12 and would be consistent with a defect that predates onset entirely, in which case the thing that changed at 05:18:31 has not been identified by any evidence here. Likewise, if the open question resolves the other way — that an unset CURRENCY_ADDR is what leaves the nil pointer in the post-processor path — then config state, not the artifact, is the mechanism, and the correct action would be to *set* CURRENCY_ADDR, which is not what revert_config would do from the current recorded state. Unblock by: retrying the metric queries with a valid expression, and re-running the trace query bounded to 05:00–05:30 on the onset date, since the returned sample was truncated at 5 of 10 and contained only 2026-10-11 06:19–06:36 traces [tr_220bfd64ac6d] — the onset cohort was never inspected.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is that checkout keeps panicking in PlaceOrder and orders keep failing while the investigation reopens the metrics and onset-trace questions; this is a live customer-facing failure and waiting has a real cost. The risk of the alternatives is worse and asymmetric: a rollback_image with no recorded prior tag either fails outright or redeploys an arbitrary image, and a revert_config here would push CURRENCY_ADDR=currencyservice:7001 onto checkout — a value the evidence rules out as present at onset — which if the post-processor nil pointer is unrelated adds a second fault on the checkout→currency edge on top of the first, and makes the next round of evidence harder to read because the config state at onset is no longer reconstructable.
proposal.blast_radius: No service is touched, so nobody sees a change. For reference, had an action been taken on checkout, the container recreate would reset connections for frontend-proxy and frontend (its callers, both already alerting) and briefly halt outbound calls to cart, currency, payment, shipping, product-catalog and email; a revert_config in particular would have moved checkout's currency traffic to currencyservice:7001, which currency — a service with no recorded change at all in the window [tr_2754c2f01980] — would have seen as a traffic shift.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on checkout followed by frontend-proxy two minutes later suggest a real user-facing failure propagating upward, with no open incident to attribute it to. No evidence yet distinguishes a checkout-side fault from a downstream dependency, so the fault class stays unknown.
